summary: Norwalk harbor-mouth light on Sheffield Island: a 1868 stone house with a cast-iron lantern, retired in 1902, lit again in 2011 as a non-navigational light.

light.characteristic: Fixed white, red flash every minute (Board list, 1899)

structures.role: keeper's house of the first light

access.note: Reached only by the Norwalk Seaport Association's ferry; tours in season.

events.note: First stone tower on the island, about thirty feet tall (LighthouseFriends: standing by mid-1827; New England Lighthouses: built 1827)
Year established per the USLHS place record; the nomination calls the first lighthouse an 1826 lighthouse
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (USLHS and New England Lighthouses give 1857; LighthouseFriends gives 1858)
Congress appropriated funds for a new lighthouse and keeper's quarters (LighthouseFriends)
Granite or gneiss house with cast-iron lantern tower completed; lens moved in from the old tower
Keeper Noah Mosher, Sr. died suddenly in July 1872 (newspaper account as quoted by LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses)
Steam propeller Pottsville wrecked and burned off the Norwalk Islands near the mouth of the harbor; crew of nine escaped unharmed. Dispatch does not tie it to the light.
Keeper Samuel A. Armour ill with typhoid after drinking water from the station cistern; his wife kept the light for about three months (New England Lighthouses)
Retired 15 February 1902 (LighthouseFriends); Greens Ledge light replaced it
Declared surplus and sold; Thorsten O. Stabell bought it (highest sealed bid per LighthouseFriends; auction under $5,000 per New England Lighthouses)
Bought by the Norwalk Seaport Association for $700,000
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, 19 January 1989
Major storm flooded the basement with over four feet of water and washed away ten feet of shoreline (LighthouseFriends). New England Lighthouses dates the flood to a fall 1993 tropical storm.
Tropical storm in the fall of 1993 sent waves against the foundation (New England Lighthouses; LighthouseFriends dates the flood to 1992)
Gabions installed and beach grass and roses planted to slow erosion near the lighthouse
Solar-powered tower light first shown 17 October 2011; not an aid to navigation, visible intermittently from the Connecticut shore
Restoration work paid for by a $250,000 state grant (LighthouseFriends)

notes_for_editor: Disputed or unresolved: (1) first light: 1826 (nomination), 1827 (LighthouseFriends mid-1827 tower; New England Lighthouses), 1828 (USLHS 'Year Established'; the record's first_lit); the story gives all three. (2) Lens: 1857 (USLHS, New England Lighthouses) vs 1858 (LighthouseFriends). (3) Stone: granite (LighthouseFriends), gneiss (nomination), limestone (USLHS for keepers' quarters). (4) First tower height: 30 ft (LighthouseFriends) vs 34 ft (nomination). (5) Discontinuance: the nomination puts discontinuance in the late 1890s but also gives operation to 1902; LighthouseFriends gives 15 Feb 1902; the story uses 1902. (6) 1914 sale: highest sealed bid (LighthouseFriends) vs auction under $5,000 (New England Lighthouses). (7) Flood: 1992 (LighthouseFriends) vs fall 1993 tropical storm (New England Lighthouses). New England Lighthouses names the storm; the name is not used in the story. (8) LighthouseFriends ties Smith's 1845 removal to 'President John Tyler', who had taken office in 1841; the dates do not fit. The story states both LighthouseFriends' removal and Connecticut History's death in 1845 as a disagreement, and gives LighthouseFriends' Tyler link as its account. (9) Armour's wife kept the light in 1901 (New England Lighthouses); no name in the sources read; not added to the roster. (10) The Waterbury item (sources 12) gives no year: '1899' is from the dispatch date and 'late Saturday night' (14 October 1899). It places the wreck off the Norwalk Islands, not at the light. (11) CT History's account of the 1840 steamboat Lexington fire 'cruising toward' this light is unsourced: no footnote ties it here. Not used. (12) Local Light-House Board reports for 1868-1890 are not in the corpus (lhb holds 1891-1901), so the 1868 building and the 1870s-1880s keepers rest on the nomination, LighthouseFriends, New England Lighthouses, CT History and the USLHS record. A check of the original reports is advised. (13) The 2011 relight is not in the record's event list; added here as 'relit'. The Advocate article gives 'more than 100 years' and '109 years'; the story uses 'more than a century'. (14) Roster matched by name and position (0.74 km); roles normalised from the USLHS headings (Principal Lighthouse Keeper = head keeper). (15) Second-hand quotations: the 1850 inspection and 1872 newspaper are quoted as New England Lighthouses gives them; the 1838 inspection, the 1893 cow story and the Gazette lines come from LighthouseFriends. (16) A 1991 ghost story from New England Lighthouses was left out: it is recollection, not a record of the station. (17) No photos added; the record's Commons image was not reviewed. (18) Connecticut History gives storm damage as the reason a country club closed on the island in 1937; New England Lighthouses gives lack of fresh water. Both are stated. (19) Board report scan pages were checked against each volume's own page order (scan page = position in the volume, counted from 0; printed page read from the page head): 1891 p.78 (printed 59), 1896 p.64 (printed 57), 1899 p.45 (printed 36), 1901 p.98 (printed 72). The 1896 and 1899 pages were wrong before this check.
